Strategy: Fuse both parents: keep parent two's preserved window [30,45] and penalized window [10,20], but grade the bonus by parent one's band parity — residuals in even 10-wide bands earn 30, odd bands earn 15 — so within the preserved window the ranking prefers residuals near 40-45 over 30-39. The penalty still discourages awkward small leftovers. Ranking changes only when residuals fall inside these windows; it may fail if the band split has no real link to future item sizes.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (30 if 30 <= r - item <= 45 and ((r - item) // 10) % 2 == 0 else (15 if 30 <= r - item <= 45 else 0)) - (25 if 10 <= r - item <= 20 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge both parents' tight-fit branches — parent one's steep slope with parent two's wider threshold of 12 — and reshape the loose branch into a bimodal rule: residuals in [13,30] lose 20, so the rule prefers either a near-exact fill or a genuinely roomy bin and avoids middle residuals that are neither tight nor useful. Ranking changes inside the penalized middle band; it may fail if middle residuals are actually the best compromise for the item stream.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(200 - 2 * (r - item) if r - item <= 12 else ((r - item) - 20 if 13 <= r - item <= 30 else (r - item))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent one's two-regime shape with parent two's windows: residuals up to 12 score 100 minus residual; looser bins score their residual, so tight fills dominate and roomy bins beat middle ones. On the loose branch, add 20 for residuals in [30,48] when the item size is 1 modulo 3, and subtract 20 for residuals in [8,22]. Ranking changes inside the windows or at the threshold; it may fail if the modulo gate has no link to item sizes.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(100 - (r - item) if r - item <= 12 else ((r - item) + 20 if 30 <= r - item <= 48 and item % 3 == 1 else ((r - item) - 20 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else (r - item)))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent one's shape with parent two's windows, gated by the open bin count: residuals up to 12 score 100 minus residual; looser bins score their residual. Only with at least 8 feasible bins do the windows apply: plus 20 for residuals in [30,48] when the item is 1 modulo 3, minus 20 for residuals in [8,22]. Ranking changes inside the windows when many bins compete; it may fail if the bin-count threshold rarely binds.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(100 - (r - item) if r - item <= 12 else (r - item)) + (20 if 30 <= r - item <= 48 and item % 3 == 1 and len(bins) >= 8 else 0) - (20 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 and len(bins) >= 8 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Combine best fit with parent two's shape, gated by item size: residuals up to 12 score 100 minus residual, so near-exact fills dominate. For looser bins, items of 40 or more score their residual, spreading them into roomy bins and sparing tight bins, while smaller items score minus residual. Ranking changes in the loose region at item size 40; it may fail if large items rarely arrive while roomy bins are open.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(100 - (r - item) if r - item <= 12 else ((r - item) if item >= 40 else -(r - item))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent one's tight-fit jump with parent two's windows over a new concave base: score is minus the square root of the residual, so differences among large residuals matter less than among small ones. Residuals up to 12 add 100, keeping near-exact fills dominant; residuals in [28,48] add 15 and residuals in [8,22] subtract 15. Ranking changes at the tight threshold and inside the windows; it may fail if compressing large-residual differences hides useful distinctions.

Ranking changes inside the peak window and among tied loose bins; it may fail if treating roomy bins alike wastes better choices.

Each term blends one feature from each parent, so ranking changes inside the windows by item size and residue; it may fail if the crossed combination fits neither parent's evidence.

Ranking changes wherever the grids disagree with best fit; it may fail if the fine slices have no link to future items.

The rule is best fit at band granularity, with window adjustments on top. Ranking changes inside bands and windows; it may fail if fine residual differences within a band actually matter.

```python

    return [-((r - item) // 10) * 10 + (25 if 30 <= r - item <= 45 else 0) - (25 if 10 <= r - item <= 20 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Outside both windows, plain best fit applies. Ranking changes inside the relative windows; it may fail if future items rarely repeat the current size.
